overall_assessment:
Hold candidate adherence closure for one remaining response-ordering defect in the changed reducer. The supplied corrections substantively resolve the previously reported fixed-editor scenarios, but omitted-resource retention uses the editor association captured when the catalogue request began. A catalogue response remains admissible after a same-channel editor switch and can consequently discard the newly selected editor's highest known observation. This is a source-supported counterexample, not an executed reproduction. No tools were called or files edited.

Decision table — candidate scope:
| Decision | Position | Evidence and limits |
| D01 | Adherent | Seller submission, owner/admin draft permissions and normal authenticated browser journeys remain preserved; no intermediate administrative approval appears. |
| D02 | Adherent | Backend definition/preview authority remains unchanged. The consumer preserves persisted fingerprints, escaped text, debounce and edit/context guards. |
| D03 | Adherent | Draft revisions, immutable submission snapshots and explicit new-draft variations retain their existing owner. No remote-edit path is introduced. |
| D04 | Adherent for the affected correction | Historical classification survives failure. The current browser sequence demonstrates normal same-account reauthorization, retained historical time, failed refresh, lower-fence current success and reload. Changed-account association remains protected. |
| D05 | Adherent on carried producer evidence | Submission authorization, durable reservation/quota coordination, captured dispatch authority and bounded provider access remain unchanged. The consumer delta introduces no additional provider request. |
| D06 | Adherent on carried producer evidence | Immutable ACK evidence remains separate from the associated remote resource. One-POST and local-certainty behavior are unchanged. Omitted unchanged submission methods are carried by the supplied hash and prior assurance, rather than independently reverified here. |
| D07 | Exception | Common eligibility and editor proof are separated for the demonstrated equal-fence and recovery cases. Finding ADH-R35-01 identifies another reachable loss of a higher known observation during page replacement. |
| D08 | Exception | Existing dirty-edit, operation-metadata, passive-read and context/editor regressions pass. ADH-R35-01 remains because catalogue adoption checks the account context while retaining an editor reference captured before a same-context selection change. |
| D09 | Adherent | Narrow template ports, scoped resolver, explicit factory registry and ChannelTransportModule reuse preserve the approved boundary. No textual Channel extension, unsupported no-op provider or generic capability platform is introduced. |
| CR-01 | Adherent on carried evidence | GETs remain observational and recovery remains explicit on the same operation, without automatic external POST replay. |
| CR-02 | Adherent on unchanged producer evidence | Typed refusal versus ambiguity semantics remain unchanged; correlation is not presented as acknowledgement. |
| AR-V11-01 | Adherent on carried evidence | Positive persistence confirmation and bounded readback remain the certainty model; the consumer correction does not change transaction or ACK behavior. |
| AR-V11-02 | Adherent on carried evidence | Global technical account coordination remains separate from scoped business definitions, operations and observations. |
| AR-V11-03 | Adherent by supplied attestations | Initial admission and current receipts report the required source comparisons, thirty protected sources and three unchanged product HEADs. Hashes were not independently recomputed in this review. |
| CR-V11-01 | Backend adherent; consumer exception | Both producers retain the shared persistent lease/fence/projector. ADH-R35-01 concerns losing newer evidence already admitted by the consumer, rather than backend write authority. |

The r35 failure correction is faithful to the approved ownership distinction. Common failure rows retain negative availability/eligibility and truthful status, time, fence and historical classification; only the individual projection receives the draft-use veto. Keeping matchesDefinition as a semantic fact is appropriate. The changed pure assertion corrects an implementation-shaped expectation without removing the common negative gates. The actual recovered browser response supplies the owned resource, APPROVED, available/eligible/matchesDefinition/eligibleForUse=true and fence 12 greater than 10 before the unchanged eligibility DOM assertion. No pass-the-test shortcut is established by this correction.

The supplied current canonical all reports exit 0 and 797 passing cases: 284 API unit, 398 PostgreSQL, 42 Web unit and 73 Playwright cases, comprising 72 browser cases and one pure consumer case. Source/runtime attestations report 38 matching sources, thirty protected seals, matching served/dist bytes and 25 disposable migrations. Both template FRC markers originate in the browser journey: 100 actual BFF calls with 99 lease responses and one completed provider leader, followed separately by 100 UI attempts coalesced into one BFF refresh. These results substantiate the executed scenarios; the newly identified editor-switch ordering is absent from those scenarios.

Historical RED limits remain bounded. r31 reached three behavioral failures; its sibling catalogue setup failure was not a behavioral RED. r32 stopped at its first composed-common assertion. r33 passed the added ordering cases but failed the existing main recovery oracle before the later FRC probes. r34 retained two causal worker failures with incomplete initial capture and a transcribed process result, not a complete first-byte log or original receipt. r35 completes the final assertions without expanding those earlier claims. The earlier r21 derived-read, r27 capture-prefix, r28 final-response and r29 first-assertion limits remain unchanged. Original feature provenance remains test-after/unknown.

Performance is acceptable for this slice. Page-first SQL bounds child hydration, detail history and catalogue probes remain bounded, and the reducer operates over loaded observations without extra HTTP, provider fan-out or another persistent cache. Existing OFFSET/count costs and bounded fixture measurements establish no production capacity or SLO. Elegance is acceptable: the small pure reducer is justified by the admitted cross-slice dependency. Its remaining retention error needs a local correction, not architectural expansion. Structural soundness and operational fit remain mixed because an editor can regress from known PAUSED to an older eligible APPROVED observation.

No new compatibility bridge or temporary architecture exception is evident. TQA-ST05-03 remains accepted historical process debt. SEC-R6-04 remains deferred through foundation_documentation/backlog/README.md#BLG-leadshug-template-recovery-read-budget, restricted to the private local cohort before separately approved public admission or Railway. Operator-confirmed credential revocation/disablement retains its stated limits; no renewed confirmation or retest is needed. Formal PCV disposition, preserved TEST preflight/migrations, source-bound activation, actual assisted Meta submission/status, module consolidation and fresh final review remain later mandatory gates. Empty-200 browser coverage and browser ACK-conflict-race coverage remain disclosed limits. Delivery remains Pending.
recommended_path: Resolve ADH-R35-01 within the existing observation owner. Add a fail-first regression covering a same-channel editor switch while an older catalogue response is held, followed by newer passive evidence for the newly selected editor and an older page response omitting that resource. Preserve exact page membership while retaining the active editor's highest observation at adoption time. Run the required validation and affected independent reassessment, then continue through the remaining candidate, PCV, activation, assisted-provider and final-review gates.

findings.title: Page replacement can discard the newly selected editor's highest observation
findings.rationale: In web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx:235, reduceTemplateObservationSlices takes selectedId from action.selectedRemoteTemplateId. refreshCatalog captures that reference from the current operation when the request starts, and loadCatalogPage carries it unchanged into the eventual action. Catalogue admission checks contextEpoch and observation intent, but a same-channel abrirRascunho changes editorEpoch without changing that account context. Consider a catalogue request started while editor A is selected, with its response held. The user opens B, whose individual projection is APPROVED at fence 300 with valid draft proof. Before the held response arrives, an admissible passive page supplies B as PAUSED at fence 301; both views correctly show PAUSED through the final merge, while individualStatus still contains B at 300. The older catalogue response then arrives with membership omitting B. Its returned items are compared against current pages, but B is absent and therefore receives no comparison. Retention still targets captured A, and the condition rejects retention because individualStatus belongs to B. The reducer discards the page containing B at 301 and leaves B at 300. mergeTemplateObservations then exposes the older APPROVED observation, potentially eligible in both views within its TTL. This directly violates D07/D08 preservation of newer known evidence. The existing omission test supplies an unchanged selected resource, and browser cases 61/62 retain the same editor throughout; neither covers this ordering. This defect is in the newly added retention path, rather than unchanged accepted debt.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): determine the active editor association at adoption time within the existing owner, and retain its highest currently known observation before replacing page membership. Preserve returned IDs, cursor and page metadata exactly; keep the retained observation in the existing individual slice. B: represent editor selection changes explicitly as metadata/events in the existing local reducer so pending catalogue actions cannot use obsolete editor ownership. Neither option needs another observation cache, endpoint or provider call. C: retain the regression as a contract exception; this is unsuitable without renewed approval because known PAUSED evidence can become eligible APPROVED. Add a pure transition with current pages containing B/301/PAUSED, individual B/300/APPROVED, and a replacement response carrying request-time selected A while omitting B. Also prove the reachable sequence through real BFF held responses and a same-channel A-to-B switch: B stays PAUSED/ineligible before and after replacement, page membership remains exact, dirty text survives and provider mutation counts remain unchanged.
